title: Dario Amodei
text:
Dario Gabriele Amodei (born January 13, 1983) is an American artificial intelligence (AI) entrepreneur and researcher. In 2021, he and his sister Daniela Amodei founded Anthropic, the company behind the large language model series Claude. Before that, he was the vice president of research at OpenAI. At US$965 billion as of May 2026, Anthropic is one of the most valuable AI pure play companies, rivaled by OpenAI.
Amodei earned a doctorate in biophysics from Princeton University. From 2014 to 2016, he worked on machine learning at Baidu and Google Brain. At OpenAI, he worked on the development of GPT-2, GPT-3, and reinforcement learning from human feedback.
Amodei has led an AI safety culture at Anthropic, and has expressed a probability of catastrophic harm from AI at 10–25%. Simultaneously, Amodei has advocated for democratic nations to maintain an AI lead to deter authoritarian nations, especially China, via advanced military AI, and semiconductor export controls. Since 2026, Amodei has also called for a slowdown of AI development, especially recursive self-improvement by democratic states, while engaging China in arms control-analogous diplomacy. Time magazine listed Amodei as one of the world's 100 most influential people in 2025 and 2026.

#Early life

Dario Amodei was born in 1983 in San Francisco, California. His sister, Daniela, was born four years later. His father, Riccardo Amodei, an Italian-American leather craftsman from Massa Marittima, Tuscany, died of hepatitis C when Dario was 23 years old. His mother, Elena Engel, a Jewish American born in Chicago, worked as a project manager for libraries.
Dario grew up in San Francisco and graduated from Lowell High School. He was a member of the USA Physics Olympiad team in 2000. Amodei began college at Caltech, where he worked with Tom Tombrello as one of his Physics 11 students. He later transferred to Stanford University, where he received a bachelor's degree in physics. He was awarded the Hertz Foundation Fellowship in 2007 while earning his doctorate in biophysics from Princeton University. He later received the Hertz Thesis Prize in 2011 for his doctoral research on the electrophysiology of neural circuits. He was a postdoctoral scholar at the Stanford University School of Medicine.

#Career

From November 2014 until October 2015, he worked at Baidu. After that, he worked at Google Brain. In 2016, Amodei joined OpenAI. He worked on the development of GPT-2, GPT-3, and reinforcement learning from human feedback.
In 2021, Dario and his sister, Daniela, founded Anthropic along with five other former senior members of OpenAI including Jared Kaplan and Chris Olah. The Amodei siblings were among those who left OpenAI due to directional differences. In November 2023, the board of directors of OpenAI approached Amodei about replacing Sam Altman and potentially merging the two startups. Amodei declined both offers.
Time magazine listed Amodei as one of the world's 100 most influential people in 2025, and again in 2026 alongside his sister Daniela. He also was named as one of the "Architects of AI" for Time's Person of the Year.
As of May 2026, Anthropic has an estimated value of $965 billion, with Forbes estimating Amodei's net worth to be $15.5 billion.
In September 2026, Amodei called for the technology industry to slow the pace of AI development and said Anthropic would allow independent evaluators permanent access to its models to assess whether the company was following its safety commitments. In Anthropic's IPO financials and prospectus release, it was disclosed that Amodei's compensation package in 2025 tallied $18 million, including stocks. Their IPO is valued at $2 trillion as of October 2026.

#Dispute with the Department of Defense

In February 2026, Amodei refused to remove a contractual ban on Claude usage for mass domestic surveillance or fully autonomous weapons, as requested by Pete Hegseth's Department of Defense (DoD). Anthropic was subsequently labeled a DoD "supply-chain risk" and the Trump administration ordered US agencies to stop using Claude. The Pentagon denied interest in such use cases but insisted on unrestricted access. The DoD's actions have been condemned as illegal retaliation against protected speech with several organizations filing amicus briefs supporting Anthropic. On March 26, 2026, a federal judge issued a temporary injunction against the DoD, agreeing that their actions appeared to be "classic First Amendment retaliation."

#Views

Amodei has promoted an AI safety culture at Anthropic, and has expressed a probability of catastrophic harm from AI at 10–25%. Amodei has advocated for democratic nations to maintain a lead in the AI arms race to deter authoritarian nations, especially China. Since 2026, Amodei has also called for a slowdown of AI development, especially recursive self-improvement by democratic states, while engaging China in arms control-analogous diplomacy.
In October 2024, Amodei published an essay titled "Machines of Loving Grace", in which he speculated about how AI could radically improve human welfare.
In January 2026, Amodei published a follow-up essay titled "The Adolescence of Technology", which focuses on the risks posed by powerful AI. According to Amodei, one possibility is that AI systems develop goals or behaviors misaligned with human intentions. Another is that he believes AI may allow people without specialized training to create biological weapons or weapons of mass destruction.
Amodei has said that AI could enable authoritarian governments to conduct unprecedented surveillance, deploy autonomous weapons, and engage in mass propaganda. He has described the Chinese Communist Party as the greatest threat in this regard, arguing that democracies must maintain AI leadership to prevent a "global totalitarian dictatorship".

#Personal life

In 2014, Amodei was diagnosed with testicular cancer and made a full recovery following chemotherapy treatment. Amodei began dating Camilla Clark in 2014 and married her in 2022. Clark has been an influential advisor to Amodei at Anthropic, and helped the company to secure investment in 2021 from her former boyfriend, Google CEO Eric Schmidt. She was also active as an entrepreneur herself and attempted in 2011 to win Jeffrey Epstein as an investor for an adult entertainment business she had founded.
